name: Asparagus
grown_as: A hardy perennial vegetable grown in a permanent bed from one-year-old crowns, cut for spears in April to June. Most modern varieties are all-male (no berries); drawn with berries on a female plant for the seed stage. ⚠️ CHECK whether William's plants are all-male.
habit: In spring: separate spears pushing up from the soil. Left uncut, each spear grows into a tall, airy, much-branched feathery stem 1 to 1.5 m, the 'fern', like a soft green cloud. Dies down in autumn.

leaf.arrangement: The true leaves are tiny brown scales on the stem. What looks like foliage are clusters of 3 to 8 needle-like green branchlets (cladodes) set at each node along the fine side branches.
leaf.type: Not true leaves: needle-like branchlets in tufts
leaf.outline: Each needle 1 to 2.5 cm long, thread-thin, round, slightly curved
leaf.base: All needles of a tuft rising from one point, above a tiny triangular brown scale
leaf.margin: None to speak of: each needle is round
leaf.colour: Fresh mid green, turning yellow then straw-brown in autumn

flower.petals: Six tepals joined into a narrow bell with the tips flaring slightly
flower.centre: Six small stamens (male) or a small green ovary (female)
flower.carried: One or two at a node among the fern on thin, jointed stalks, hanging down. Male and female flowers on different plants.

fruit: On female plants only: round berries 6 to 10 mm, green turning bright red, hanging singly from the fern on thin stalks, each with 1 to 6 black seeds. Seeds round, black, about 3 to 4 mm. The berries are poisonous.
winter: Fern turns yellow, then brown, and is cut down to a few cm; nothing above ground but stubs and mulch

leaf: fine branches carrying tufts of 3 to 8 needle-like green branchlets
bloom: a tiny narrow bell of six tepals
hanging on a thin jointed stalk
crown: a central crown with budded tips
many long thick fleshy roots spread out like a spider
crop: separate green spears coming straight out of the soil
tight scale leaves lapped at each tip, purple-tinged
growing: a soft cloud-like look, no broad leaves
seedhead: among the green or yellowing fern
dormant: bare soil with short cut stubs
or yellow-brown dying fern before cutting

look_alikes: Wild asparagus by the sea (Asparagus prostratus) is low and sprawling. Asparagus 'fern' (Asparagus setaceus) is a houseplant with flat sprays. Fennel and dill have true feathery leaves with sheathing stalks and yellow umbels.
